value.hook: Read when giving a docs-system verdict on a .dd/schemas/pij change: validate live docs and fixtures in a scratch repo, never in the shared review worktree.
value.title: Verdict a schema change against the live documents

sections.name: body
sections.value:
For a C7 schema verdict (first used on PR #135, the pij/role state and merged_into fields), the questions are: does every live document still validate, does each fail fixture fail for the stated reason, and are the project docs clean and their renders current.

What worked, with no build and without touching the review worktree (other seats share it, so never move its HEAD or write in it):

1. `S=$(mktemp -d)`, then `git -C <review worktree> archive <head> .dd | tar -x -C $S`, then `git init` in `$S`. ddocs needs a git repo with `.dd/` at its root, or it reports E401 (schema not found).
2. Copy in every committed `roles/*/role.dd.json` from the governance worktree plus the schema's fixtures, `git add` them (an untracked target only WARNs), then run `ddocs validate --depth 0 --json` on each. Read `.error.details.issues[].message` for the reason: a fail fixture should fail with exactly one issue, at the field the fixture is about.
3. Probe what ddocs cannot express. It has no conditional or union rules, so "field X only when state is Y" never fails in ddocs. Write one probe document that breaks the pairing; if it validates, the writer has to hold the rule. Then read the code paths that write the document (add --file, edit --file, the verbs) to see whether they do.
4. For project docs: `git archive <head> .dd docs/project` into a second scratch repo, commit it, `ddocs validate` and `ddocs build` each file, and check `git status` is clean. Clean means the committed .dd.md renders are current.

Also check what a roadmap step's done_when promises against the steps it depends_on. On #135, s15 promised "a send refuses", but role sends belong to s05, which is still planned.
